support.quote: Here, we implement a toy model of this duality called the HaPPY code, a quantum error-correcting code in the form of a tensor network with hyperbolic entanglement patterns, on a trapped-ion quantum computer. We present the first experimental confirmation of the Faulkner-Lewkowycz-Maldacena formula in this model - a key test of the holographic correspondence.

canonical_record.label: Nearly simultaneous arrival of widely separated photon energies from GRB 090510
canonical_record.summary: NASA reports that two photons from GRB 090510, differing in energy by a factor of one million, arrived at Fermi nearly simultaneously after traveling more than 7.3 billion light-years.

support.quote: Fermi-LAT was able to test this using photons from the bright GRB 090510. Two of the photons, one a million times more energetic than the other, traveled over 7.3 billion light-years before arriving at the telescope, arriving at nearly the same time, thus demonstrating that Lorentz invariance holds strong.

canonical_record.label: GRB 090510 constraint on energy-dependent light speed
canonical_record.summary: NASA reports that GRB 090510 placed a strong constraint on variation of light speed with photon energy, with high- and low-energy gamma rays arriving within one second after traveling approximately seven billion light-years.

canonical_record.label: Fermi GBM detector coverage and burst detection rate
canonical_record.summary: NASA describes the Fermi Gamma-ray Burst Monitor as having 14 detectors covering the unobscured sky, detecting approximately 240 gamma-ray bursts per year across an energy range of 8 keV to 40 MeV.

support.quote: The Gamma-ray Burst Monitor (GBM) has 14 detectors (12 lower-energy sodium iodide crystal scintillators, 2 higher-energy bismuth germinate scintillators) that together cover the full unocculted sky and detect ~240 bursts per year with spectral coverage from 8 keV - 40 MeV.
